title: Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objective · abstract-1-1】The visual field (VF) test results of many eyes with glaucoma progress despite treatment. This suggests that some eyes are either untreated or that the management of intraocular pressure does not influence the outcome. In this work, we explore whether future VF parameters can be predicted from a baseline OCT-retinal nerve fiber layer (OCT-RNFL) scan using a deep learning model.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Design · abstract-2-1】Retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation.

【Methods · abstract-4-1】A Vision Transformer (ViT)-based regression model was trained on baseline OCT-RNFL scans to predict 3 key VF indices (follow-up interval: 4.74 ± 2.59 years). Model performance was evaluated using regression metrics with 95% confidence intervals. Saliency maps were generated to identify OCT-RNFL regions for making decisions in predicting functional visual status.

evidence.text: Retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation.

A Vision Transformer (ViT)-based regression model was trained on baseline OCT-RNFL scans to predict 3 key VF indices (follow-up interval: 4.74 ± 2.59 years). Model performance was evaluated using regression metrics with 95% confidence intervals. Saliency maps were generated to identify OCT-RNFL regions for making decisions in predicting functional visual status.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-6-1】The model achieved MAE of 3.23 (2.91-3.56), 1.76 (1.61-1.93), and 1.14 (1.03-1.27) for future VFI, MD, and PSD in internal validation, with comparable performance in external data sets (Zeiss OCT: 3.19 [2.73-3.66], 1.92 [1.69-2.16], and 1.11 [0.95-1.29]; Heidelberg OCT: 4.14 [3.82-4.46], 2.71 [2.51-2.91], and 1.37 [1.21-1.55]). The corresponding RMSE values reflect similar trends across the internal and external data sets. Saliency maps revealed that the inner and outer RNFL layers were key structures in driving the model's predictions.

【Conclusions · abstract-7-1】Our ViT-based regression model effectively predicts key future VF indices objectively from a single OCT-RNFL scan, with strong performance across 2 OCT devices, offering a novel tool for predicting functional visual status.

The corresponding RMSE values reflect similar trends across the internal and external data sets. Saliency maps revealed that the inner and outer RNFL layers were key structures in driving the model's predictions.

Our ViT-based regression model effectively predicts key future VF indices objectively from a single OCT-RNFL scan, with strong performance across 2 OCT devices, offering a novel tool for predicting functional visual status.
